text: **Where this sits:** The project [[slnc 150]] `fifty-shades-of-dotfiles` . The job [[slnc 150]] `speak-clipboard` , the key that reads the clipboard aloud. The step [[slnc 150]] saving the pause work and bringing its documentation up to date, now finished. **What it means for you:** everything behind today's pause changes is now in the repo, not in a temp folder that disappears. The follow-ups that wait on you or on later work are in open items. Three things done. Saved, not pushed. **Pause measurements saved.** done low risk. The before and after runs of the example, the punctuation table, the silence-command sweep, and the label and number trials are now in the repo. `chars.py` now holds the full silence-command sweep, from 0 to 1000 ms, so the table can be measured again. **Discovery.** The saved results held the full path of the script they measured, which includes your user name. The leak check stopped the commit, and those paths now start with `~` . **Note.** `pauses.py` now writes paths starting with `~` too. **Note.** The recordings (`.wav`) were not kept. Running `pauses.py` again makes a new one. **Proof.** No user name or temp path is left in those files, checked against a control word found 123 times. **Proof.** The leak scan over this session's two commits passed, after its own control passed. **Design doc updated.** done low risk. Its title now names the pauses and the lead-in, as well as profiles. It points to the saved results and says which result backs which ruling. A new "Known limits" part names four limits: - Only Aaron at 440 wpm was measured. - The measuring tool can mix up two pauses that are close together. - Its recordings have no lead-in. - The lead-in isn't heard yet. **Follow-ups filed.** done needed low risk. W-20261012-A12 (does the 300 ms lead-in stop the missing first words): waits on your ears. W-20261012-A13 (lines in the render log have no time): an old error can't be told from a new one. **Needed.** Press the speak key a few times after a quiet spell, on the Bose headphones, and listen for the first word. **How to undo it:** One command removes the saved results and the doc changes: ``` git -C ~/CODE/Scaffoldings/fifty-shades-of-dotfiles revert --no-edit 5b7523b. ``` **Left behind [[slnc 150]]** the two open items stay open until closed by hand. **Context:** **The saved results [[slnc 150]]** `~/CODE/Scaffoldings/fifty-shades-of-dotfiles/docs/reference/speak-clipboard-pauses/results/` , 19 small files, one per measuring run. **The design doc [[slnc 150]]** `~/CODE/Scaffoldings/fifty-shades-of-dotfiles/docs/SPEAK_CLIPBOARD_PROFILES.md` , sections "Pauses (v9)" and "Known limits". **`5b7523b` :** the commit for the saved results and the doc. `5b8b481` holds the script change itself. **`/pj:wrap-up` :** the end-of-session command. It writes the handoff that the next session reads first. **Type `/pj:wrap-up` when you're done for now, or press the speak key and tell me how the start sounds.**
